title: Kyverno Policies
description: Inventory, readiness and compliance of every Kyverno policy, legacy and CEL. Source: components/kyverno-dashboard in cluster-configurations.

panels.title: Policies
panels.description: Policy objects of every kind, legacy and CEL.

panels.title: Legacy
panels.description: kyverno.io: ClusterPolicy, Policy, ClusterCleanupPolicy, CleanupPolicy.

panels.title: CEL
panels.description: policies.kyverno.io: ValidatingPolicy, MutatingPolicy, ImageValidatingPolicy, GeneratingPolicy, DeletingPolicy and their namespaced variants.

panels.title: Not ready
panels.description: Policies Kyverno reports as not ready. A policy that is not ready is not applied.

panels.title: No status
panels.description: Policies of kinds for which Kyverno writes no readiness at all (DeletingPolicy, NamespacedMutatingPolicy and the cleanup policies in Kyverno 1.18). Normal for those kinds, not a fault.

panels.title: Fail-open
panels.description: Policies with failurePolicy Ignore. When Kyverno does not answer in time, the request is admitted without them and nothing reports it. Watch Kyverno health when this is above zero.

panels.title: Objects failing
panels.description: Distinct objects failing at least one policy, from PolicyReports. ReplicaSets are not counted; their Deployment carries the same result.

targets.expr: count(count by (resource_kind, resource_namespace, resource_name) (kyverno_ksm_report_result{result=~"fail|error", resource_kind!="ReplicaSet"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Kyverno down
panels.description: Kyverno controllers Prometheus cannot scrape. With the admission controller down, policies with failurePolicy Ignore stop being applied without any error.

panels.title: $legacy_kind
panels.description:
Every legacy policy of this kind.

Ready: Kyverno's readiness for the policy. "No status" means Kyverno writes no readiness for this kind, not that the policy is broken.

Problem: why a policy is not ready, from its status conditions.

Mode: Enforce blocks requests; Audit only reports.

Webhook: Fail-open (failurePolicy Ignore) means a request is admitted without this policy whenever Kyverno does not answer in time.

Objects evaluated / failing: distinct objects in PolicyReports for this policy. An object fails when any rule fails or errors. Click a failing count to filter the Failing objects table.

panels.title: $cel_kind
panels.description:
Every CEL policy of this kind.

Ready: Kyverno's readiness for the policy. "No status" means Kyverno writes no readiness for this kind, not that the policy is broken.

Problem: why a policy is not ready, from its status conditions.

Mode: Enforce blocks requests; Audit only reports.

Webhook: Fail-open (failurePolicy Ignore) means a request is admitted without this policy whenever Kyverno does not answer in time.

Objects evaluated / failing: distinct objects in PolicyReports for this policy. An object fails when any rule fails or errors. Click a failing count to filter the Failing objects table.

panels.title: Failing objects per policy
panels.description: Distinct failing objects per policy, now, from PolicyReports.

panels.title: Failing objects over time
panels.description: Distinct failing objects per policy over the selected range. A step up after a rollout is a regression; a step down is a fix landing.

panels.title: Failing objects
panels.description: Every object that fails or errors a policy rule, from PolicyReports. Messages of rules that errored start with "ERROR:". Filter with the Policy and Namespace variables at the top.

targets.expr:
1000 * (
  (label_replace(label_join(kyverno_ksm_report_result{result=~"fail|error", resource_kind!="ReplicaSet", resource_namespace=~"$namespace", policy=~"$policy"}, "result_message", ";", "result", "message"), "message", "ERROR: $1", "result_message", "error;(.*)")
    * on (source, policy) group_left (policy_kind) kyverno:policy_info)
  or on (source, policy, rule, resource_kind, resource_namespace, resource_name)
  label_replace(label_join(kyverno_ksm_report_result{result=~"fail|error", resource_kind!="ReplicaSet", resource_namespace=~"$namespace", policy=~"$policy"}, "result_message", ";", "result", "message"), "message", "ERROR: $1", "result_message", "error;(.*)")
)

panels.title: Requests denied, by policy
panels.description: Admission requests refused by an Enforce (legacy) or Deny (CEL) policy. A refused request never reaches the cluster, so it is in no PolicyReport.

targets.expr:
60 * sum by (policy_name) (rate(kyverno_validating_policy_execution_duration_seconds_count{execution_cause="admission_request", result="fail"}[$__rate_interval]))
  and on (policy_name) max by (policy_name) (kyverno:policy_info{policy_family="cel"} * on (policy_id) group_left () (kyverno:policy_enforce:state == 1))

panels.title: Requests denied, by resource
panels.description: Every admission request Kyverno refused, whatever the policy type.

panels.title: Violations admitted (Audit), by policy
panels.description: Admission requests that failed an Audit policy and were let through. Clear these before switching a policy to Enforce.

targets.expr:
60 * sum by (policy_name) (rate(kyverno_validating_policy_execution_duration_seconds_count{execution_cause="admission_request", result="fail"}[$__rate_interval]))
  and on (policy_name) max by (policy_name) (kyverno:policy_info{policy_family="cel"} * on (policy_id) group_left () (kyverno:policy_enforce:state == 0))

panels.title: Mutations applied, by policy
panels.description: Requests a mutating policy changed at admission.

panels.title: Admission review latency
panels.description: Time Kyverno adds to each API request it reviews. It counts against the API server's webhook timeout.

panels.title: Slowest policies (p95)
panels.description: Per-policy execution time, admission and background scans together.

panels.title: Scrape targets
panels.description: Kyverno controllers, and kyverno-state-metrics, which feeds every table above.
